items.1: Kvit keeps your name, your groups, expenses and payments, and your personal budget if you make one. Email accounts also keep an email and a scrambled password.
items.2: Your data is used only to run Kvit. It is never sold, and there are no ads and no tracking.
items.3: People in your group see that group's expenses. Nobody else does, except the person who runs Kvit if a group is reported.
items.4: You can download your data and delete your account in Settings.

1.heading: Who runs Kvit
1.body: Kvit is run by Filip Davchev in North Macedonia, as a free project for family and friends. He decides how your data is used. Contact: kvit.support@gmail.com.

2.heading: What Kvit keeps
2.body: Your name, language and time zone. For an email account: your email and a scrambled form of your password. For Google sign-in: your email, the link to your Google picture and Google's ID for you. The groups, expenses, payments and notes that you and your friends enter, and your personal budget if you use it. Simple counts of how the app is used, tied to your account but never with amounts or names. A guest keeps only a name and what the guest enters.

3.heading: Why Kvit uses it
3.body: To run your account, your groups and your budget (this is what you ask Kvit to do). To keep Kvit safe, stop abuse and limit too many tries (a legitimate interest: keeping a free service working). To count how many people use Kvit (also a legitimate interest, with counts only).

4.heading: Who can see what
4.body: People in a group see that group's expenses, payments and balances. Your personal budget is seen only by you. The person who runs Kvit sees only totals, for example how many accounts exist. If someone reports a group or an account, he can look at what he needs to decide, and he keeps a note of what he did and why.

5.heading: Companies that help run Kvit
5.body: Cloudflare delivers the website and passes requests on. Render runs the server. Neon stores the database. Google handles sign-in if you use it. These companies process data only to give their service to Kvit. The National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia only receives requests for exchange rates, with no personal data.

6.heading: Data outside the EU
6.body: The database is in Frankfurt, Germany. Cloudflare, Render and Google are US companies and may handle data outside the EU. They say they use approved safeguards, such as the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or standard contractual clauses.

7.heading: Sign in with Google
7.body: The Google button loads a script from Google when the first screen opens, so Google can see your internet address and browser details even if you don't tap it. If you sign in, Kvit receives your name, email and picture link. Kvit cannot read your Gmail, your contacts or anything else in your Google account.

8.heading: Passwords
8.body: A password is never stored the way you type it, only as a scrambled code that nobody can turn back into the password.

9.heading: In your browser
9.body: One login cookie keeps you signed in for 90 days, and Kvit needs it to work. Your phone or browser also keeps a saved copy of your screens so they open fast, a queue of changes waiting to be sent, and your language and theme. The saved copy is cleared when you log out. No ads, no tracking cookies.

10.heading: How long Kvit keeps things
10.body: Your data stays while your account exists. When you delete your account it is switched off at once and removed within 30 days. A deleted group or expense can be restored for a while, and is removed 30 days after that. Single usage events are merged into monthly totals after 12 months. The companies above keep technical logs for a short time, from days to a few weeks. Kvit's database can be restored up to 6 hours back, and Kvit keeps an encrypted weekly backup for up to 90 days. Accounts that are not used are kept and are not deleted automatically.

11.heading: If someone added your name
11.body: Someone in a group may type your name to add you, for example for a shared trip. Kvit keeps that name and the group's expenses in that group only. If you don't want to be there, write to kvit.support@gmail.com with the group link, and we will take your name out or replace it with “Former member”.

12.heading: Your rights
12.body: You can ask to see your data, correct it, delete it, limit its use, get a copy, or object to its use. You can also complain to the Personal Data Protection Agency of North Macedonia, or to the authority where you live.

13.heading: Download your data
13.body: In Settings, tap “Download my data”. You get a file with your profile, your personal budget and your groups with their expenses and payments. It does not contain other people's emails or private budgets.

14.heading: Delete your account
14.body: In Settings, tap “Delete my account”, or write to kvit.support@gmail.com. Your account is switched off at once. If you log in again within 30 days, the deletion is cancelled. After 30 days your email, login, Google link, password, personal budget and sessions are removed. Guests can delete their account too.

15.heading: What stays after deletion
15.body: Expenses and payments in your groups stay, because other people's balances depend on them. Your name stays on them, or shows as “Former member” if you choose that when you delete. The saved copy and the queue in your own browser are removed when you log out. Backups can hold your data for up to 90 days.

16.heading: Do you have to give data?
16.body: To make an account you give a name, and for an email account also an email and a password. Without them Kvit can't work for you. A guest gives only a name.

17.heading: No automated decisions
17.body: Kvit makes no decisions about you by computer and does no profiling. Your data is not sold.

18.heading: Age
18.body: Kvit is for people aged 16 and over.

19.heading: Changes
19.body: If this notice changes, the date and version at the top change and you see a notice in the app.

items.1: Kvit is a notebook for sharing expenses with friends and family. It does not hold, send or receive money.
items.3: Amounts and exchange rates can be wrong. Check them before you rely on them.
items.4: Kvit is free and comes with no promises: it can be slow, change or stop, and data can be lost.
items.5: What you write is yours. Be fair to other people, or your account can be suspended.

1.heading: Who can use Kvit
1.body: Kvit is for people aged 16 and over. If you are younger than 16, please don't make an account or join a group.

2.heading: Your account
2.body: You are responsible for everything that happens with your login. Keep your password to yourself. A guest has no email, so if a guest loses the phone or the browser, the account can't be recovered. Tell us if someone else is using your account.

3.heading: A notebook, not a bank
3.body: Kvit only keeps a record of who paid and who owes. It does not hold, send or receive money, and it does not make anyone pay. “Paid” and “confirmed” mean what the people in the group say. Pay each other outside Kvit, the way you always did.

4.heading: Amounts, rounding and rates
4.body: Kvit rounds amounts and changes euros and denars with the exchange rates of the National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia. Rates can be late or wrong, and rounding can leave small differences. Kvit gives no financial, tax or legal advice.

5.heading: How to use Kvit
5.body: Don't use Kvit to harass, threaten or cheat anyone, to share illegal content, to pretend to be someone else, to send spam, or to try to break or overload it.

6.heading: What you write
6.body: The names, amounts and notes you enter stay yours. By entering them you let Kvit store them and show them to the other members of your group, so that the app can work.

7.heading: Between members
7.body: Disagreements about money or anything else in a group are between its members. Kvit is not a party to them and can't settle them.

8.heading: No promises
8.body: Kvit is free and offered as it is. It can be slow, stop, change or lose data, with or without warning. Keep your own copy of anything important: you can download your data in Settings.

9.heading: Responsibility
9.body: As far as the law allows, the person who runs Kvit is not responsible for losses that come from using Kvit or from not being able to use it. This does not limit anything that the law does not allow to be limited.

10.heading: Suspending and removing
10.body: Kvit can suspend an account or close a group that breaks these Terms or that someone reports, and can remove content. You can delete your own account at any time in Settings.

11.heading: Changes
11.body: If these Terms change, you will see a notice in the app, and the date and version at the top change. For big changes we ask you to agree again. If you keep using Kvit after a change, you accept the new Terms.

12.heading: Open-source parts
12.body: Kvit is built with open-source software, and each part keeps its own licence. The name Kvit and Kvit's own code are not offered for reuse.

13.heading: Contact
13.body: Questions, reports and requests about these Terms or your data: write to kvit.support@gmail.com.

14.heading: Law and courts
14.body: These Terms follow the law of North Macedonia, and its courts decide disputes about them. This does not take away any right that the law gives you as a consumer where you live.

15.heading: If a part does not apply
15.body: If one part of these Terms is not valid, the rest still applies. Nothing in these Terms removes a right that the law gives you.
